chapter: Keppard, Oliver and the Magnolia band
title: Freddie Keppard and the trumpet at Huntson Nagel's
summary: The 101 Ranch band was strings only; brass was illegal in the District until Keppard played and Parker got a permit, creating the Magnolia band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Ten years. Ten years. You played that quite a while. Yeah. The other night you mentioned the first time that Freddie Peppard came by and played with you. Was that at Parker's? Can you tell us about that again?

No, that was at the 101 Ranch. We only had string instruments there. And first Minetta was on the piano, then John Bean was on the drum. Old man Bean, Tarcum, on the drum. And I was playing the guitar then. Wasn't I playing? Yeah, I was playing the guitar then. And then we had the old man Willie O'Pri on the clarinet, sax. And we didn't have nothing. We had Jimmy Pala on the violin. Jimmy Pala. I got Jimmy for you. Yeah, you got Jimmy for you.

And then after, a little running come in. Yeah. Old man officer got a running and he had the boys, what they call him, he packs up his instrument. The gold's art. And you went behind and crossed the 25 and that was old John. That was George. That guy right.

And then, yes that's right. Now then they, then after we got Freddie, Freddie came in from a job. He played a job on his trunk. Well they wasn't, they didn't have, they didn't allow no blowing instruments.
It was against the law, was it?

It was against the law to blow brass instruments in the district. So, uh, Harry Parker asked me what instrument was that and I told him a trumpet. So he said, well tell him to play something. And he said, oh boss I can't play nothing, it's a violation of the law. I'm afraid, but if you protect me, I'll play. He said, well I'll, I'll protect you. He said, go ahead, there ain't nobody gonna do you nothing. So he blowed his trumpet and right after that he asked, it sounds so good he asked me, do you think you can get that fella to play a regular? I said, well I'll, he said, I'll go see the mayor and get a permit. I believe you told us the other night that all the women came from the, her birthday women. Yeah, all, that was at the, at Ponson Nagels. Was that across the street or? No, the next block at Liberty, Liberty in, in, in, uh, And they heard Freddie playing. And they heard the band of Freddie was playing the trumpet that, that drawed all of them over there because they had never heard a trumpet, you see. And, uh, well then after Harry Parker went to the mayor and got a permit to have, to have a blowing instrument, that made the Huntson Nagel then go hard your arms up there, you see. Full band, the Magnolia band, that was the name of the band at that time. Well he had a full band, about six or seven pieces then.
Previously that was all string band.
